newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin senators face recall over abortion vote.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin senators face recall over abortion vote.

text.p: Anti-abortion activists were confident Monday they would collect enough signatures by Tuesday's deadline to force a recall vote on Wisconsin's two Democratic U.S. senators.

The activists, grouped in a Milwaukee-based organization called First Breath Alliance, were seeking an unprecedented statewide recall vote for Senators Russ Feingold and Herb Kohl because of their opposition to federal legislation banning so-called "partial birth" abortions.

The bill, banning the procedure used to end some late-term pregnancies, passed both houses of Congress, but did not receive enough votes in the U.S. Senate last month to override a veto by President Clinton.
To reach the recall phase, supporters must obtain 391,000 valid signatures against each senator and turn them in to the state Elections Board by Tuesday at 5 p.m. CDT (6 p.m. EDT).
"We're confident we can make it," alliance founder Norbert Nicholas, a Cedarburg insurance executive, said. He said the group had collected about 300,000 signatures by the weekend.

Opponents of the effort have labeled the whole enterprise illegal. The U.S. Constitution does not address the issue directly, legal experts said, but courts have held states cannot set regulations for electing members of Congress.
Leaders of the pro-life alliance said the 10th Amendment -- the one that reserves to the states powers not delegated to the federal government -- gave them a legal foothold.
"That clearly reserves recalls to the states, and Wisconsin has provided for recalls of elected officials," alliance spokesman Bill Kling said.
Regardless of the legal jousting, the state elections board was getting prepared to verify as many as one million signatures.
Even if the recall election never took place, several political observers said the drive was hurting Feingold, whose first six-year term expires next year.
His leading political opponent, Republican Rep. Mark Neumann, was encouraging the recall even though he said he has no connection to it.
